Subject: Multi-jurisdiction deployment check-in: Sakura Finance private grid

Hi Liam —

Thanks again for walking us through Sakura Finance's compliance constraints earlier this week. To make sure the engineering review is focused, can you confirm the following items so we can finalize a deployment option and an acceptance checklist?

- Primary residency constraints: which datasets MUST remain in-region (EU-only, JP-only)?
- KMS / HSM requirements: must the key material be managed by Sakura or can Redwood integrate with an in-region KMS?
- Failover expectations: acceptable RTO / RPO for cross-region failover for tenant traffic?
- Networking: any egress restrictions or approved peerings (e.g., direct connect, partner interconnect)?
- On-prem presence: confirm whether your Tokyo PoP will host dedicated GPUs or just network edge routing.

I've attached a short questionnaire (sakura-initial-network-questions.pdf) — if you can fill the highlighted fields we will route to engineering and produce a recommended topology (dual private clusters vs. single-control with regional isolation).

Proposed next step: 30-minute follow-up Thursday to walk the topology options with legal and platform engineering. Is 10:00 JST / 02:00 UTC workable?

Best,

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-12-04T18:12:00+09:00
Subject: Re: Multi-jurisdiction deployment check-in: Sakura Finance private grid

Marissa —

Thanks, attached is a quick matrix (sakura-network-constraints.xlsx) with our high-level legal requirements. Summary follows:

- Data residency: Payment tokens and PII must remain within the EU for EU customers; APAC transactional logs and certain telemetry must remain in Japan. Cross-border replication for analytics is allowed only after anonymization and with written consent.
- KMS: We must manage customer-facing key material inside region via our on-prem HSM in Tokyo and a separate KMS cluster in Frankfurt for EU. Redwood may integrate but key material cannot be escrowed off-site.
- Failover: For customer-facing inference, our legal team is comfortable with a warm-standby model: RTO goal 5 minutes, RPO up to 30 seconds for session state; critical audit trails must be retained in-region at all times.
- Network: No outbound egress to third-party analytics outside the region unless approved. We have an existing private interconnect from Tokyo PoP to our primary data center; EU will be peered with Redwood Dedicated via an S2S VPN to Frankfurt.
- On-prem: The Tokyo PoP will host accelerated inference hardware (NVIDIA A100 equivalent) and will accept containerized Redwood Private nodes — we can provide rack-level acceptance windows.

Questions back to you:
- How do you recommend we handle KMS proxies for the control plane without moving key material?
- What level of prefix-based routing isolation can Redwood support between EU and APAC tenant traffic?

We can do Thursday 10:00 JST. I attached the constraints sheet.

Cheers,
Liam O'Connor
EngOps, Sakura Finance
liam.o@sakurafinance.jp
Attachment: sakura-network-constraints.xlsx (stub)

Forwarding Liam's constraints. Short internal summary and suggested options:

TL;DR: We need regionally isolated custody for PII/payment tokens, in-region KMS that Sakura controls, warm-standby RTO 5m / RPO 30s, and strict egress controls.

Options to propose (pros/cons):
- Option A: Dual private deployments (FRK + NRT) with per-region tenant pinning
  - Pros: Clear legal separation, local KMS integration, lowest compliance risk
  - Cons: Higher infra cost, replication complexity for non-PII data

- Option B: Single private control plane (EU-hosted) with regional data planes and strict network ACLs
  - Pros: Lower control-plane overhead, easier rollout management
  - Cons: KMS proxy complexity, may raise legal flags unless we implement strict zero-knowledge controls

Questions for Jonas/infra:
- Can Redwood Private run a lightweight in-region control-plane proxy that never sees key material (just session coordination)?
- What are the network egress guardrails we can bake into the deployment template (BGP communities, route filters)?

I'll draft a short acceptance checklist to include with either option. Attaching my notes.

Thanks,
Naomi

Subject: Re: Multi-jurisdiction deployment check-in: Sakura Finance private grid — proposed topology and runbook

Hi all —

Appreciate the clear constraints. Based on the requirements, here's a recommended deployment pattern and the acceptance/runbook items we'll use for the SOW:

Recommended topology (high level):
- Phase 1 (Compliance-first): Dual private clusters — Frankfurt (EU) + Tokyo (APAC). Each cluster owns its resident datasets and local KMS.
- Control plane: Customer-managed private control plane in EU for EU tenants; a lightweight control-plane proxy in APAC handles scheduling and health-checks but never stores keys or PII.
- Replication: Asynchronous, application-layer replication for non-PII material only. Session-state replication uses encrypted KV streams with per-region keys; critical audit logs are written locally and exported on request (never replicated without anonymization).

Network & peering requirements:
- BGP peering between Sakura PoPs and Redwood-managed egress nodes. We will publish a prefix set per-cluster and support route filters/BGP communities to prevent accidental cross-border egress.
- Enforce egress via IP ACLs and TLS SNI allowlist; no third-party analytics egress by default.
- S2S VPN to Frankfurt for management plane; direct private interconnect to Tokyo PoP for data plane.

KMS & key flow:
- Integrate with Sakura's on-prem HSMs using KMIP/YubiKey-based attestation where supported. Redwood will provide a KMS adapter that proxies requests but never exports key material. All crypto ops for sensitive tokens occur in-region.

Failover behavior:
- Warm standby: Tokyo and Frankfurt can promote locally; in event of EU outage, EU traffic fails over to EU backup nodes (if available) or to degraded mode in APAC per contract (requires legal consent).
- RTO/RPO: Default RTO 5 minutes / RPO 30 seconds for session state; tests required during cutover.

Acceptance / cutover checklist (high-level):
1) Network acceptance: BGP adjacencies validated, ACLs in place, traffic egress tests passed.
2) KMS integration: test sign/verify flows with Sakura HSMs, key attestation reports.
3) Data residency test: synthetic traffic that simulates EU customer records and validates no cross-border persistence.
4) Failover drill: perform coordinated warm-standby promotion with rollback within target RTO.
5) Audit: collect evidence (pcaps, logs, KMS attestations) into shared drive for legal review.

Attachments: runbook stubs (sakura-deploy-runbook.md, network-acl-template.json). I've also linked the draft design doc: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2b3C4d_sakura-deploy-design and the HubSpot record HS-789012 for tracking.

- Marissa: confirm Thursday 10:00 JST meeting and invite legal/infra.
- Naomi: please iterate the acceptance checklist into the SOW template; I will draft the network ACL language.

I'll schedule the call once Liam confirms.
